clue.text: Take a chance in selection, given last word for a change

indicators.note: the two words are to be altered, their letters set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks at random and lets the final say on the matter swing the choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' shuffles the eight letters of LAST and WORD; 'given' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide something by picking slips or straws at random is to leave the choice to luck.

clue.text: Thoroughly examine and torture a pair of partners imprisoned

indicators.note: the torture device locks the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the rack was an instrument of torture, and to rack is to torture
North and South are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: Two people are jailed, interrogated and tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners, giving NS.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly, turning everything over.

clue.text: Sea creature swallows sole, swimming in huge quantities

indicators.note: the whale gulps down the fish, so it is the container

parts.note: a whale is a sea creature

indicators.note: swimming means the fish's letters move about

explanation.surface: A whale gulps down a swimming flatfish in vast amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as the fish but is just anagram fodder: 'swimming' scrambles it, and 'swallows' puts the result inside the whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale trade deals in bulk, large quantities.

clue.text: Old people left inside shrine

indicators.note: inside shows the letter for left sits within the people

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: Elderly people abandoned within a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a shrine where a god's prophecies were given, as at Delphi.

clue.text: Overnight, I slink off, being such a shy person

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away during the night, being timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is a very timid, retiring person.

clue.text: Wonder if poet has finally lost money

indicators.note: the poet's name drops something from its very end, so 'finally' places the loss

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a seventeenth-century English poet
L stands for the pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a poet has ended up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Marvell's surname ends in a double L; dropping the last L (the pound sign, money) leaves the word for wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is a wonder, something astonishing; as a verb it also means to wonder at.

clue.text: Doctors having gone on round found carrier of disease

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so doctors are MOs
to have quit is to have gone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Medics on their rounds discover what is spreading an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosquitoes transmit malaria and other diseases.

clue.text: Judgment made by composer about time

parts.note: Verdi was an Italian composer
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A ruling given by a musician roughly on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a jury's decision or judgment.

clue.text: Start to recognise something hereditary in girl's size

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl, the 's being a link

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a gene carries hereditary traits

explanation.surface: Beginning to see an inherited trait in a girl's build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' is the first-letter signal on 'recognise'; the girl's 's is possessive and gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness is bigness, how great something's size is.

clue.text: Marketplace accepting new sort of goat

indicators.note: the marketplace takes in a letter, so it acts as the container

parts.note: an agora was the marketplace of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: A market takes in a novel breed of goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of goat prized for its long silky mohair fleece.

clue.text: Relax heartless command for one who returns

parts.note: to relax is to rest

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: an order is a command

explanation.surface: Telling someone to take it easy, minus the bossiness, aimed at a person coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle D out of ORDER, leaving ORER.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer brings something back to its former condition, returning it to how it was.

clue.text: Explorer's incomplete claim rejected in island

indicators.note: the reworked claim sits inside the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: rejected, as in sent back, means the shortened word is read backwards
incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to allege is to claim

explanation.surface: An explorer's partial assertion is dismissed on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts ALLEGE to ALLEG; 'rejected' turns it to GELLA, which goes inside MAN. The 's of 'Explorer's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail round the world.

clue.text: Revolting team's taken advantage

parts.note: people up in arms are revolting, in revolt
a side is a team, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A rebellious squad has seized the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means in revolt, not disgusting: the people are UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside of something is its benefit or good aspect.

clue.text: Seabirds see another one returning on board

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the steamer holds the bird

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword's usual ship to be on board

indicators.note: returning means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: an auk is another seabird

explanation.surface: Seabirds spot a second bird coming back to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for being inside SS (steamship); 'returning' turns AUK to KUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Skuas are large predatory gulls of the open ocean.

clue.text: Party activity finds growing support around shopping centre

indicators.note: around means the plant's support encloses the shopping centre

parts.note: a stalk supports a growing plant
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a cane round a shopping precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Small talk is the light chat of social gatherings.

clue.text: Parasite that traditionally overlooks displays of affection

definitions.text: Parasite that traditionally overlooks displays of affection

parts.words: Parasite that traditionally overlooks displays of affection
parts.note: a plant living on trees that is hung up at Christmas so that couples kiss beneath it

explanation.definitionFit: This semi-parasitic plant is hung overhead at Christmas, and custom says people under it should kiss.

clue.text: Rivalry from Greek character accepted in good mood

indicators.note: the Greek letter is taken into the mood, so the mood is the container

parts.note: elation is high spirits
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Competition from a Greek who is welcomed cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulation is the effort to equal or surpass another, a form of rivalry.

clue.text: Sin that subverts real duty

indicators.note: subverts means overturns, so the letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: A sin that undermines one's true obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery, infidelity in marriage, is a sin under the commandments.

clue.text: Saw covering page by writer as something extra

indicators.note: the saying wraps round the other pieces, so it is the outer piece

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A cutting tool laid over a page beside a pen, as an extra bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a proverb, not the cutting tool, and 'covering' makes it the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is an addition attached to something larger, such as a limb.

clue.text: Brown is after place as tradesman

indicators.note: the colour comes after the place, giving the order of the pieces

parts.note: umber is a brown pigment

explanation.surface: A man called Brown is chasing a position as a workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a skilled tradesman who fits pipes.

clue.text: Break one's skin

parts.note: to cut is to break, as in a cut in power
one is I, and the 's gives S

explanation.surface: A fall cuts someone's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, especially its deeper layer.

clue.text: Don, perhaps, from African country lacking capital

indicators.note: the capital is the opening letter, which goes

parts.note: someone from Liberia, in West Africa, is Liberian

explanation.surface: A university teacher who apparently hails from an African nation without its capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is the first letter, L, not a city. Don is the Spanish title for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gentleman, titled Don, comes from the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Barwoman's wine, excellent when brought up

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: A1 is excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A barmaid's drink, very fine, is served upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barwoman' means a woman at the Bar, a lawyer, not a barmaid. AI, A-one, is first class.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia disguises herself as a lawyer to argue in court.

clue.text: False allure of poetry prize

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: The deceptive glamour of winning a prize for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A laurel wreath crowned poets in ancient times, hence the Poet Laureate.

clue.text: One heavily criticised about nothing and taken apart

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: about means round, so the criticism surrounds the nothing

parts.note: to slate is to criticise severely
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone savaged for making a fuss over nothing, then pulled to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated is set apart and cut off from others.

clue.text: Living off the land

parts.note: not foraging, but dwelling up in trees, away from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal creatures live in trees, above and off the ground.

clue.text: Of dusky appearance?

parts.note: describing something seen in the half-light at dusk rather than something dark-skinned

explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit only by the dim light after sunset.

clue.text: Woollen material from pullover initially altered

indicators.note: only the first letter of the garment's name is changed for another

parts.note: a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A cloth made from a sweater that was changed at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially altered' swaps the J of JERSEY for a K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kersey is a coarse ribbed woollen cloth, named after a Suffolk village.

clue.text: Rehearsal of Suite in G

parts.note: a suite is a retinue of attendants, a train
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A practice run of a piece of music in the key of G.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' looks musical, but it is a retinue, a TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is practice and preparation, like rehearsing.
